newsitem.title: USA: ICE HOCKEY-GORDIE HOWE SIGNS TRYOUT CONTRACT WITH AHL SYRACUSE.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-GORDIE HOWE SIGNS TRYOUT CONTRACT WITH AHL SYRACUSE.

text.p: Ice hockey icon Gordie Howe, regarded by many to be the greatest player in the history of the sport, is planning a return to professional hockey at the age of 69.
Howe, who retired from the National Hockey League in 1980 at 52, signed a tryout contract with the Syracuse Crunch of the American Hockey League (AHL), the team announced Friday.

Howe, who stayed in the pros long enough to play alongside his sons Mark and Marty with Houston of the defunct World Hockey Association (WHA) and the Hartford Whalers, will begin training immediately.
"Although at the age of 69 I may appear to be what is termed 'poetry in slow motion', it's exciting and challenging to see how I might squeeze into the Crunch lineup," Howe said.
The Hall of Famer and Detroit Red Wings legend is expected to make his AHL debut when the team hosts the Carolina Monarchs April 1.
"It won't be easy.... Maybe I'll have to sharpen my elbows just a little bit more," he joked. "It's fun to be a possibility thinker and to have (my wife) Colleen do another contract for me."

Howe, who earned the nickname Mr Hockey in 26 remarkable NHL seasons, is second all-time to Wayne Gretzky with 801 career NHL goals. Including his years in the WHA, Howe has scored 1,071 career goals and amassed 2,589 points.
The 1996-97 season commemorates the 50th anniversary of Howe's first pro contract with the Red Wings in 1946-47.
"Somehow I can't believe Gordie really wants to do this, but we'd all love to see Gordie back on the ice again," said Colleen Howe.
"My role has always been to give support to whatever Gordie wants to do, and it's no different now."
